text: Before Nvidia became the company that supplies most AI training hardware, what did it originally sell?
explanation: Nvidia started in 1993 selling graphics chips for PCs, and the near-bankruptcy of 1996 over a failed product line is the turning point most people miss. The CUDA bet that followed is what turned a gaming hardware firm into the supplier of the AI industry.

text: The AI bubble is a term for a stock market phenomenon said to have been growing since when?
explanation: Since 2025, amid the AI boom, and the argument is that leading firms are in a circular flow of investment that inflates each other's valuations. Ray Dalio has drawn comparisons with earlier bubbles, and the interesting part is that the sceptical case is about capital structure rather than about the technology being useless.

text: Google acquired DeepMind in 2014. Roughly what did it pay?
explanation: Reportedly around 400 million pounds, for a company four years old whose main public achievement was a Go program that beat Lee Sedol four games to one. The price looked steep in 2014 and looks like a rounding error against what AlphaGo and AlphaFold did for the acquirer, which makes it the clearest example of AI acquisitions being mispriced before 2023.

text: Who is credited with the 1965 observation that transistor counts double roughly every two years?
explanation: Gordon Moore, who wrote it while running Fairchild Semiconductor and later co-founded Intel. He described it as an empirical observation rather than a law, and the half dozen names on this list all worked at Fairchild or Intel, which is the trap in the question.

text: Boston Dynamics, the robotics firm, has been owned since 2020 by which group?
explanation: Hyundai Motor Group, which began the acquisition in December 2020 and completed it in June 2021. Boston Dynamics was founded in 1992 as a spin off from MIT, and the humanoid and dog robots became a meme long before they were anywhere near useful on a factory floor.

text: Paul Allen founded the Allen Institute for AI using money earned from which other company?
explanation: Microsoft, where Allen was the co-founder with Bill Gates. He also funded the Allen Institute for Brain Science, and both institutes are a useful reminder that a large share of American research infrastructure is paid for by one person's money rather than by grants.

source.title: Allen Institute for AI
source.label: Allen Institute for AI on Wikipedia

text: After Microsoft's 2019 investment, which cloud platform became OpenAI's exclusive provider for a time?
explanation: Microsoft put in $1 billion in 2019 and Azure became OpenAI's exclusive cloud for a time. Amazon Web Services is the tempting miss because it is the largest cloud overall, but it never held the OpenAI exclusivity. OpenAI has since spread compute across more partners, including the Stargate venture, so the exclusivity belongs to that 2019 era.

text: Bard's February 2023 demo error wrongly credited which telescope with taking the first pictures of exoplanets?
explanation: The Bard promo claimed the Webb telescope took the very first exoplanet images, wiping about $100 billion off Alphabet's value in a day. Hubble is the tempting miss because it is the famous space telescope, but the actual first images came from the Very Large Telescope in 2004.

text: Which startup did Databricks agree to acquire for about $1.3 billion in June 2023?
explanation: Databricks bought MosaicML for its MPT models and efficient training stack so enterprises could build models on their own data. Anthropic is the tempting miss because it also raised billions in 2023, but its backers were Amazon and Google, not Databricks.

text: Which company hired most of Inflection AI's team and licensed its technology in March 2024?
explanation: Mustafa Suleyman and Karen Simonyan moved to lead Microsoft AI, taking most of the Inflection staff with them in a deal that drew regulator scrutiny. Google is the tempting miss because Suleyman co-founded DeepMind there, but the 2024 acquihire went to Microsoft.

text: Which trio of companies created the Stargate venture announced in January 2025?
explanation: Stargate was announced at the White House as a $500 billion, four-year AI infrastructure buildout starting in Texas. The Microsoft, Nvidia and xAI trio is the tempting miss because all three are key technology partners, but the equity founders were OpenAI, SoftBank and Oracle plus MGX.

text: Whom did Elon Musk sue in early 2024 over OpenAI allegedly abandoning its founding mission?
explanation: Musk filed in February 2024 claiming OpenAI betrayed its nonprofit charter by chasing profit and keeping models closed under Microsoft's influence. The Amodei and Anthropic pairing is the tempting miss because Anthropic is also an OpenAI splinter, but Musk sued Altman, Brockman and OpenAI.

text: Which company announced a $6 billion Series B funding round in May 2024?
explanation: Musk's xAI raised the $6 billion from Valor, Andreessen Horowitz and Sequoia to build Grok products and compute capacity. Mistral AI is the tempting miss because it also raised a huge 2024 round in Europe, but the May 2024 $6 billion Series B was xAI's.

text: Which biometric does the Orb built for World scan to issue a World ID?
explanation: The chrome Orb photographs irises to prove unique personhood without storing who you are, the core of Sam Altman's Tools for Humanity project. Face is the tempting miss because the Orb looks like a Face ID camera, but the identifier it derives is an iris code.

text: In June 2026 the Commerce Department ordered Anthropic to cut off foreign nationals from its two newest Claude models. Why did that leave Fable 5 and Mythos 5 switched off for everybody?
options: Anthropic could not check users' nationality in real time
The models needed retraining before anyone could run them
Amazon withdrew the compute both models were running on
The directive also banned Anthropic's US-based employees
answer: Anthropic could not check users' nationality in real time
explanation: The directive landed at 5:21pm ET on 12 June 2026 and covered any foreign national anywhere, including Anthropic's own staff, so the only way to comply was to switch both models off for every customer; Commerce lifted it on 30 June. Retraining is the tempting miss because the models were fine, and Amazon is the tempting miss because an Amazon researcher's report about a safeguard bypass is what set the directive off.
answerAliases: no reliable way to verify nationality in real-time

text: In September 2026 Oracle sent a force majeure notice about Project Jupiter, a Stargate data center campus in New Mexico. What was Oracle trying to achieve?
options: Delay payments if the campus slips past 2028
Buy extra capacity once the campus comes online
Cancel its lease as the campus's main tenant
Hand the campus to another Stargate partner
answer: Delay payments if the campus slips past 2028
explanation: A force majeure notice lets a tenant pause payments if the building is late, so Oracle was buying room on Project Jupiter rather than walking away from a 2.45 gigawatt campus it wants. The site is designed to run on Bloom Energy gas fuel cells, and the Energy Transfer pipeline meant to feed it slipped to February 2027 after regulators repeatedly denied permits.

source.label: TechCrunch on Oracle's force majeure notice for Project Jupiter

text: In August 2026 Nvidia licensed Poolside's Model Factory and made job offers to 109 of its engineers, in a deal the investor letter insisted was neither an acquisition nor an acquihire. Which open-weight model family would they work on?
explanation: The engineers had built Poolside's Laguna code model, and Nvidia ships its own open-weight models under the Nemotron name, the same give-away-the-tools play as CUDA. Poolside's three founders stayed on and the investor letter stressed the deal was not an acquisition, which is how this kind of deal avoids the regulatory reviews a real takeover brings.

source.label: The Decoder on Nvidia licensing Poolside's Model Factory

text: In September 2026, which Beijing AI lab confidentially filed for a Hong Kong IPO, aiming to raise $3 billion in the offering?
explanation: Moonshot AI, the developer of the Kimi models, filed confidentially on 3 September 2026 and is working with Goldman Sachs and CICC on the offering. Z.AI, formerly Zhipu, and MiniMax both listed in Hong Kong earlier in 2026, which makes them the tempting misses, while DeepSeek has never filed.

source.label: Business Times on Moonshot's confidential Hong Kong IPO filing

text: In September 2026 AMD agreed to acquire the San Francisco lab behind Fei-Fei Li, which builds models that generate and simulate 3D worlds. Which company is it?
explanation: AMD bought the lab behind spatial-intelligence models that generate and simulate 3D worlds from text and video, and Fei-Fei Li joins as executive vice president and chief scientist reporting to Lisa Su. Cognition and Anysphere are the tempting misses because both sell AI coding agents; Skild AI builds robot foundation models, not world models.

source.label: AMD newsroom on the World Labs acquisition

text: In July 2026 Nvidia announced a long-term partnership with Ilya Sutskever's lab SSI, alongside an investment in it. Which Nvidia platform did the deal hand SSI access to?
explanation: SSI said access to the Vera Rubin platform would lift its compute by an order of magnitude, and Nvidia got rare access into the lab's research in return, a swap that moves frontier demand onto its own silicon. Hopper is the tempting miss because it is the architecture behind the H100, but SSI had been running on Google TPUs before this.

source.label: TechCrunch on the SSI and Nvidia partnership

text: In September 2026 Anthropic signed a seven-year, $11.6 billion cloud contract with Akamai. Unusually for a frontier lab, what was the capacity for?
options: Nvidia GPUs for large model training
Google TPU capacity in US regions
explanation: Agent workloads are pulling demand for ordinary processors, which is how a CDN company could land a contract this size, and Akamai even handed Anthropic a warrant for up to about 5 percent of its stock. GPUs are the tempting answer because every earlier AI cloud deal sold accelerators, and Trainium is Amazon silicon, not Akamai's.

source.label: TechCrunch on the Akamai and Anthropic cloud contract

text: In July 2026 Travis Kalanick's industrial AI company Atoms raised $1.7 billion led by Andreessen Horowitz. Which company put money into the round, having forced him out as CEO in 2017?
explanation: Uber ousted Kalanick as CEO in 2017 after harassment and discrimination complaints, then took a cheque in the company he rebuilt out of CloudKitchens and Pronto; he called the round unfinished business, with a16z's Ben Horowitz joining the board. Lyft is the tempting miss because it is the ride-hailing rival a player expects, and Grab is the other founder-oustering story.

text: The EU AI Act's duties for general-purpose AI models have applied since August 2025, but for a year no one could be fined for breaking them. From what date in 2026 did the Commission's enforcement powers start?
explanation: The GPAI obligations in Articles 53 to 55 applied from 2 August 2025, and the Commission's enforcement chapter arrived a year later on the same calendar date, so providers got one grace year to assemble documentation, a copyright policy and training-data summaries. The 2026 AI Omnibus pushed the high-risk rules to December 2027 but left this date untouched.

source.label: European Commission on the AI Act framework

text: In early 2026 the Pentagon designated Anthropic a supply-chain risk, and a federal judge set that designation aside in August 2026. What had Anthropic refused to allow?
options: Any use of Claude by intelligence agencies
Sales of Claude to defence contractors
explanation: The Defense Secretary wanted Claude for all lawful purposes and Anthropic held out against mass surveillance of Americans and fully autonomous weapons; Hegseth's designation was the first time a US company was publicly labelled a supply-chain risk, and Judge Rita Lin set it aside in August 2026. Intelligence agencies are the tempting miss because the demand was not agency-specific.

source.label: NBC News on the judge blocking the Pentagon's Anthropic blacklisting

text: Three Mile Island's Unit 1 had been shut since 2019 because cheap natural gas had made it unprofitable. In September 2024 Microsoft signed a deal about it. What did Microsoft actually agree to?
options: A 20-year commitment to buy the plant's power once it restarts
Ownership of the reactor, which Constellation would run for it
Most of the $1.6 billion cost of restarting the plant
A share of Constellation Energy in exchange for the power
answer: A 20-year commitment to buy the plant's power once it restarts
explanation: Constellation shut Unit 1 in 2019 and said in September 2024 it would spend $1.6 billion to restart it by 2028, renaming it the Crane Clean Energy Center. Microsoft took no ownership and no equity; it signed a 20-year agreement to take as much of the plant's electricity as possible, because a data center wants power around the clock rather than only when the sun is up. Unit 2, the unit damaged in the 1979 accident, stays dormant.

source.title: Three Mile Island Nuclear Generating Station
source.label: Three Mile Island Nuclear Generating Station on Wikipedia

answerAliases: 20-year agreement to purchase as much electricity as possible from the plant
the entirety of the plant's energy output will be sold to Microsoft Corporation

text: In 2024 Google agreed to take as much as 500 MW of power from Kairos Power, a company building a reactor design that has never yet run commercially. What is Kairos building?
options: A large pressurized water reactor of the standard three-loop design
A gas-cooled reactor using ordinary light water as its coolant
A small modular high-temperature reactor cooled by molten fluoride salt
A molten salt reactor with the uranium dissolved straight into the fuel
answer: A small modular high-temperature reactor cooled by molten fluoride salt
explanation: The salt is a coolant, not the fuel: Kairos burns TRISO particles held in solid graphite pebbles, so what it is not is the classic liquid-fuel molten salt design. Google's 2024 agreement covers up to 500 MW from six or seven units, the first due around 2030, and none of them has Nuclear Regulatory Commission approval yet.

text: Vertiv has become one of the biggest winners of the AI buildout, even though it never trained a model or made a chip. What does it actually sell?
options: The GPUs that train large models
Power and cooling gear for data centers
Ethernet switches that link the racks together
Lithography machines that print features on chips
answer: Power and cooling gear for data centers
explanation: Vertiv began in 1946 as Capitol Refrigeration Industries, and Ralph Liebert built the first computer-room precision air conditioner in his garage, so it is really a cooling company that also sells the electrical half of a data center. Its lineup now runs from racks and busbars to uninterruptible power supplies and thermal management, and in 2023 its share price rose 252 percent, more than any other company in the S&P 500.
answerAliases: AC and DC power management, thermal management

text: Arista Networks grew into Cisco's most annoying rival in data-center switches, and in December 2014 Cisco sued it for patent infringement. How did that fight end?
options: Cisco sold Arista the patents outright in the end
An import ban that blocked Arista's switches in the US
A cross-licensing deal covering both product lines
Arista paid Cisco $400 million to settle in 2018
answer: Arista paid Cisco $400 million to settle in 2018
explanation: The International Trade Commission upheld an import ban on some of Arista's switch features, which was a real threat to a company that had only listed in 2014. The ban came down in 2016 after Arista changed the products and two patents were overturned, but the fight ran on until August 2018, when Arista paid $400 million to end Cisco's claims, drop its own antitrust case and agree to a five-year stand-down.
answerAliases: Arista agreed to pay Cisco US$400 million
Arista agreed to pay Cisco US$400 million as part of a settlement

text: By 2025 CoreWeave, Lambda, Crusoe and Nebius were routinely grouped together as neoclouds. What do those companies sell that sets them apart from the hyperscalers they compete with?
options: They sell data center space to other operators to fill
They sell rented GPU compute as their main product
They sell custom-designed AI accelerator chips to clouds
They sell hosted frontier models as a pay-per-token API
answer: They sell rented GPU compute as their main product
explanation: AWS, Azure and Google Cloud sell dozens of product lines with GPUs as one item among many, while a neocloud sells GPU compute and little else, which is why the Uptime Institute measured an on-demand Nvidia DGX H100 at roughly a third of the hyperscaler price in 2025. CoreWeave even brands itself the AI Hyperscaler in its own press releases, which is the joke. Lambda, the smallest of the four, calls itself the AI developer cloud and sells one-click GPU clusters next to single-GPU instances.

source.label: Network World on neoclouds versus hyperscalers

text: CoreWeave, the Nvidia-powered GPU cloud, was a different company in 2017. What was it doing then?
options: Renting GPUs to researchers, as a startup called Lambda
Trading bitcoin for clients, as an exchange called Coinbase
Trading natural gas futures, as a hedge fund called Hudson Ridge
Mining ethereum, as a crypto startup called Atlantic Crypto
answer: Mining ethereum, as a crypto startup called Atlantic Crypto
explanation: Founded in 2017 as Atlantic Crypto, it mined ethereum with the same graphics cards it now rents out, and when the 2018 crash made those cards cheap it renamed itself CoreWeave in 2019 and started leasing that inventory as cloud computing instead. Its founder Michael Intrator had been running Hudson Ridge, a natural gas hedge fund. Lambda is the tempting miss because it was already renting GPUs to researchers years earlier.

text: In July 2025 CoreWeave agreed to buy a bitcoin mining company that had pivoted to AI data centers. Which company was it?
explanation: A Bitcoin miner that filed for Chapter 11 at the end of 2022 and emerged in January 2024, Core Scientific signed about $10 billion of data center contracts in 2025 and was agreed at US$9 billion. Cipher Mining and Hut 8 made the same pivot from bitcoin to AI hosting, which is why they are the tempting misses. What CoreWeave wanted was the buildings and the grid connections somebody else had already paid for.

text: Nebius, the Amsterdam-based AI infrastructure company that also owns Avride and TripleTen, was created by a forced sale in July 2024. Which company did it get separated from?
explanation: Nebius was the Dutch holding company that owned Yandex, the structure Russian law required for foreign ownership, until sanctions forced it to sell the Russian business to a consortium of Russian investors in July 2024 for a discounted US$5.3 billion. What stayed outside Russia, notably the Finland data center, was rebranded Nebius and pointed at AI infrastructure. Tinkoff and Avito are Russian finance and classifieds businesses that stayed inside Russia.

text: Crusoe, one of the neoclouds now building AI data centers, was founded in 2018. What was its original business?
options: Operating a bitcoin mining pool for retail investors
Selling natural gas to hyperscale data center campuses
Licensing AI accelerator designs to server makers
Capturing flared natural gas to power its own computing
answer: Capturing flared natural gas to power its own computing
explanation: The founding idea was to capture the natural gas that oil and gas sites burn off at the wellhead and run generators on it, which Crusoe calls Digital Flare Mitigation; bitcoin mining was the first way to spend that cheap power and the AI data centers came later. The mining pool and chip licensing options describe businesses that sit either side of Crusoe's actual one. It sold the bitcoin mining business to NYDIG in 2025 to concentrate on AI infrastructure.

text: In which year did Microsoft make its first $1 billion investment in OpenAI?
explanation: Microsoft put $1 billion into OpenAI in July 2019 and made Azure its exclusive cloud for a time. The 2017 misses date the partnership too early, before GPT-2 had even shown the scaling bet could pay.

text: Microsoft extended its OpenAI partnership in January 2023 with a multiyear, multibillion-dollar deal. About how much had Microsoft put in cumulatively by that point, according to contemporaneous reporting?
explanation: The January 2023 extension was reported as a $10 billion tranche on top of the earlier $1 billion plus $2 billion, totaling about $13 billion. The $4 billion figure belongs to Amazon's Anthropic commitment later that year, not Microsoft.

text: Which Twitch co-founder served briefly as interim CEO of OpenAI during the November 2023 leadership crisis?
explanation: Emmett Shear took the interim job on November 19 2023 after Mira Murati's brief stint, then left when Altman returned days later. Nadella is the tempting miss because he hired Altman into Microsoft during the same weekend, but he never ran OpenAI.

text: On which date in November 2023 did OpenAI's board remove Sam Altman as CEO?
explanation: The board announced Altman's removal on November 17 2023, saying he had not been consistently candid. November 20 is the tempting miss because that was the weekend's chaotic middle, when Microsoft announced Altman would join it, before his reinstatement on November 22.

text: Which OpenAI co-founder quit in protest after the November 2023 firing of Sam Altman, then returned days later?
explanation: President Greg Brockman resigned hours after Altman's removal and came back when Altman was reinstated. Sutskever is the tempting miss because he voted to fire Altman, then publicly regretted it, but he did not quit that weekend.

text: During the November 2023 OpenAI crisis, who announced that Sam Altman and Greg Brockman would join Microsoft to lead a new AI research group?
explanation: Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella announced the move on November 20 2023, before Altman's reinstatement made it moot. Suleyman is the tempting miss because he later led Microsoft AI, but in 2023 he still ran Inflection.

text: After the 2019 restructuring, which body kept ultimate control of OpenAI?
explanation: OpenAI added a capped-profit arm in 2019 but left the nonprofit board in charge, which is why that board could fire the CEO in 2023. Microsoft is the tempting miss because it invested billions, but it held no board seat at the time.

text: Which company committed up to $4 billion to Anthropic starting in September 2023?
explanation: Amazon started with $1.25 billion in September 2023 with an option up to $4 billion, making AWS Anthropic's primary cloud. Google is the tempting miss because it separately put in $2 billion the next month.

text: Which company committed $2 billion to Anthropic in October 2023, shortly after Amazon's investment?
explanation: Google committed $2 billion in October 2023, split between an upfront payment and a later tranche. Amazon is the tempting miss because its larger $4 billion deal came first the prior month.

text: After the September 2023 deal, which cloud became Anthropic's primary provider for training and deployment?
explanation: The Amazon deal made AWS the primary cloud for Anthropic's training and deployment, including Trainium and Inferentia chip access. Google Cloud is the tempting miss because Anthropic also uses it under its separate Google partnership.

text: Which social platform did xAI acquire in an all-stock deal in March 2025?
explanation: xAI acquired X in March 2025, reuniting Grok with its main distribution channel under one Musk company. Reddit is the tempting miss because it also licenses data for AI training, but it was never acquired.

text: In which city did xAI build its Colossus supercomputer cluster in 2024?
explanation: xAI assembled Colossus in Memphis in 2024 with about 100,000 Nvidia H100 GPUs for Grok training. Austin is the tempting miss because Tesla and X have a large presence there, but the flagship cluster went to Memphis.

text: In which city was Mistral AI founded in April 2023?
explanation: Arthur Mensch, Guillaume Lample and Timothee Lacroix founded Mistral in Paris in April 2023 after leaving DeepMind and Meta. London is the tempting miss because DeepMind sits there, but the founders chose Paris.

text: About how much did Mistral AI raise in its Series B round in June 2024?
explanation: Mistral raised about 600 million euros in June 2024 led by General Catalyst, months after a 385 million euro round. The 105 million euro figure was its earlier 2023 seed, Europe's largest at the time.

text: Which Mistral model leaked via a torrent link in December 2023 before its official release?
explanation: Mixtral 8x7B, a mixture-of-experts model, appeared through a torrent link in December 2023 and was confirmed days later. Mistral Large 2 is the tempting miss because it was a bigger 2024 launch, but it had a normal announcement.

text: About how much did Safe Superintelligence raise in September 2024, months after its founding?
explanation: SSI raised about $1 billion in September 2024 from Andreessen Horowitz, Sequoia and others before showing any product. The $6 billion figure belongs to xAI's 2024 Series B, not SSI.

text: About how much did Thinking Machines Lab raise in July 2025 in a round led by Andreessen Horowitz?
explanation: The July 2025 seed round was about $2 billion, an unusually large first raise for a lab with no shipped product. The $6 billion figure belongs to xAI's 2024 rounds, not Thinking Machines.

text: Who founded MosaicML, which Databricks acquired for about $1.3 billion in June 2023?
explanation: Naveen Rao founded MosaicML in 2021 after selling his prior chip startup Nervana to Intel. Delangue is the tempting miss because he co-founded Hugging Face, a different open-model company.

text: In which year was Scale AI founded by Alexandr Wang and Lucy Guo?
explanation: Wang and Guo founded Scale in 2016 to sell labeled data for training AI. The 2019 options confuse it with later self-driving data deals that made Scale prominent.

text: In June 2025 Meta agreed to invest about how much in Scale AI alongside hiring Alexandr Wang?
explanation: Meta's June 2025 deal was about $14.3 billion for a 49 percent stake, with Wang joining to run superintelligence work. The $1.3 billion figure belongs to Databricks buying MosaicML in 2023.

text: What is Scale AI's core business that made it valuable to Meta and model labs?
explanation: Scale sells human-labeled data for training and evaluating models, including work for self-driving and defense customers. Cloud GPUs are the tempting miss because neoclouds sell those, while Scale sells the labels that go into training.

text: Where was the Stargate AI infrastructure venture announced in January 2025?
explanation: Stargate was announced at the White House on January 21 2025 as a $500 billion four-year buildout by OpenAI, SoftBank and Oracle. Davos is the tempting miss because big funds often announce there, but this one was a White House event.

text: Which Texas city hosts the first Stargate data center campus, under construction from 2025?
explanation: The first Stargate campus is in Abilene, Texas, where Oracle and Crusoe-linked builds were already underway. Dallas is the tempting miss because it is Texas's better-known data center hub.

text: Who was named chairman of the Stargate venture at its January 2025 launch?
explanation: SoftBank's Masayoshi Son was named Stargate chairman, with OpenAI handling operations. Altman is the tempting miss because he fronted the announcement, but the chair role went to Son.

text: In which month and year did Nvidia first pass $1 trillion in market value?
explanation: Nvidia crossed $1 trillion in May 2023 on AI chip demand, the first chipmaker to do so. January 2024 is the tempting miss because that was when it passed larger milestones on the way to $3 trillion.

text: Which Nvidia supercomputer did Jensen Huang hand-deliver to OpenAI in August 2016?
explanation: The DGX-1 was Nvidia's first deep-learning supercomputer, delivered to OpenAI in 2016 with Elon Musk present. The H100 and A100 versions are the tempting misses because they power modern clusters, but they came years later.

text: In what year did Nvidia launch CUDA, the programming platform behind its AI dominance?
explanation: Nvidia launched CUDA in 2006, letting researchers program GPUs for general computing well before deep learning took off. The 2012 option marks the AlexNet moment that made CUDA essential, not its launch.

text: Which networking company did Nvidia acquire in 2019 for its InfiniBand interconnects?
explanation: Nvidia bought Mellanox in 2019, gaining the InfiniBand networking that links GPUs in AI clusters. Arista is the tempting miss because it competes in data-center switches, but the InfiniBand deal was Mellanox.

text: Which chip designer did Nvidia agree to buy in 2020, then abandon the deal for in February 2022?
explanation: Nvidia agreed to buy Arm from SoftBank for about $40 billion in 2020 and walked away in February 2022 under regulatory pressure. Qualcomm is the tempting miss because it also licenses Arm designs, but it was never the target.

text: What is TSMC's business model that distinguishes it from Nvidia and AMD?
options: Makes chips for others without own brand
answer: Makes chips for others without own brand
explanation: TSMC is a pure-play foundry that manufactures chips designed by others and sells none under its own brand. Selling lithography tools is ASML's business, which is why that option traps readers who mix up the supply chain.

source.title: Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company
source.label: Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company on Wikipedia

text: What does ASML, the Dutch company critical to AI chips, actually sell?
explanation: ASML is the sole maker of extreme ultraviolet lithography machines that print advanced chips. DRAM is the tempting miss because memory is also a chip business, but ASML sells the machines that make chips, not chips themselves.

text: In which country is ASML, the sole maker of extreme ultraviolet lithography machines, headquartered?
explanation: ASML is headquartered in Veldhoven in the Netherlands and grew out of a Philips joint venture. Taiwan is the tempting miss because TSMC buys its machines, but the maker is Dutch.

text: In which US state did TSMC announce new chip fabs in 2020?
explanation: TSMC announced its Arizona fabs in 2020, later expanded with CHIPS Act support. Texas is the tempting miss because Samsung and others build there, but TSMC's flagship US site is Arizona.

source.title: Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company
source.label: Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company on Wikipedia

text: Which GPU neocloud listed on Nasdaq in March 2025?
explanation: CoreWeave listed on Nasdaq in March 2025 after growing from crypto mining into rented GPU compute. Nebius is the tempting miss because it also trades publicly, but it arrived via the Yandex split, not a 2025 IPO.

text: To which firm did Crusoe sell its bitcoin mining business in 2025 to focus on AI data centers?
explanation: Crusoe sold the mining operation to NYDIG in 2025 so it could concentrate on AI infrastructure powered by stranded gas. Marathon and Riot are the tempting misses because they are large miners, but the buyer was NYDIG.

text: Which small modular reactor developer partnered with Amazon in October 2024 for up to 500 MW of nuclear power?
explanation: Amazon backed X-energy in October 2024 alongside Energy Northwest projects to power data centers. TerraPower is the tempting miss because Bill Gates backs it, but the Amazon deal was X-energy.

text: Which Illinois nuclear plant did Meta contract with Constellation for 20 years starting in June 2025?
explanation: Meta signed a 20-year deal for the Clinton plant's output starting in 2027, mirroring Microsoft's Three Mile Island agreement. Braidwood is the tempting miss because it is also a large Illinois Constellation plant, but the Meta contract names Clinton.

text: Who chaired OpenAI's initial new board formed when Sam Altman returned in November 2023?
explanation: Former Salesforce co-CEO Bret Taylor chaired the new board with Summers and D'Angelo. Summers is the tempting miss because his appointment drew headlines, but the chair was Taylor.

text: Which Georgetown research center did OpenAI board member Helen Toner direct during the November 2023 ouster?
options: Center for Security and Emerging Technology
answer: Center for Security and Emerging Technology
explanation: Toner directed Georgetown's Center for Security and Emerging Technology, whose AI-safety work reportedly strained relations with Altman. The other centers are real Georgetown units, which is why generic-center guessing fails.
answerAliases: Center for Security and Emerging Technology

text: Which board member was the only one to remain on OpenAI's board through the November 2023 firing and the reconstituted board?
explanation: Quora CEO Adam D'Angelo stayed on both the board that fired Altman and the Taylor-chaired board that brought him back. Sutskever is the tempting miss because he also survived the weekend, but he left the board in the reset.

text: In which month of 2024 did Ilya Sutskever announce his departure from OpenAI?
explanation: Sutskever announced his exit on May 14 2024, a day after the GPT-4o launch, then founded SSI in June. August is the tempting miss because Schulman's departure came then.

text: What problem was OpenAI's Superalignment team, created in July 2023, set up to solve?
explanation: Superalignment was charged with steering AI systems smarter than humans, co-led by Sutskever and Leike until it was disbanded in May 2024. Cheaper inference is the tempting miss because OpenAI also chased that, but it was never Superalignment's mandate.

text: Which lab did Jan Leike join after leaving OpenAI in May 2024?
explanation: Superalignment co-lead Jan Leike joined Anthropic in May 2024 to continue alignment work. DeepMind is the tempting miss because Leike had the safety background DeepMind hires, but he chose Anthropic.

text: Which lab did OpenAI co-founder John Schulman join after leaving OpenAI in August 2024?
explanation: Schulman joined Anthropic in August 2024 to work on alignment, then moved to Thinking Machines in 2025. SSI is the tempting miss because Sutskever founded it, but Schulman's first stop was Anthropic.

text: Who succeeded Ilya Sutskever as OpenAI chief scientist in June 2024?
explanation: Jakub Pachocki, who led GPT-4 development, became chief scientist in June 2024. Zaremba is the tempting miss because he is another Polish co-founder, but the promotion went to Pachocki.

text: What role did Mustafa Suleyman take at Microsoft in March 2024 after leaving Inflection AI?
explanation: Suleyman became CEO of Microsoft AI in March 2024, bringing Karen Simonyan and most of Inflection's staff. Azure hardware is the tempting miss because Microsoft AI also ships Copilot, but Suleyman's title was CEO of the AI division.

text: What was the name of Inflection AI's consumer chatbot released in 2023?
explanation: Inflection's Pi was pitched as a personal AI companion in 2023 before the team moved to Microsoft. Copilot is the tempting miss because it is Microsoft's assistant, but Inflection's product was Pi.

text: In which month of 2024 did Emad Mostaque resign as CEO of Stability AI?
explanation: Mostaque resigned in March 2024 to pursue decentralized AI, with Prem Akkaraju succeeding him. June is the tempting miss because leadership churn continued into the summer, but the resignation was March.

text: Which company licensed Character.ai's technology for about $2.7 billion in August 2024, with its founders rejoining?
explanation: Google licensed Character.ai's tech in August 2024 and brought back Noam Shazeer and Daniel De Freitas to work on Gemini. Microsoft is the tempting miss because it did the similar Inflection deal, but Character.ai went to Google.

text: Which company licensed Adept AI's technology in June 2024 and hired its CEO David Luan?
explanation: Amazon licensed Adept's agent technology in June 2024 and hired Luan into its AGI organization. Google is the tempting miss because it hired Character.ai and Windsurf talent in similar deals, but Adept went to Amazon.

text: What did Sam Altman's crypto-identity project Worldcoin rebrand itself as in October 2024?
explanation: Worldcoin rebranded to World in October 2024 as it pushed the Orb-verified World ID beyond crypto. Orbcoin is the tempting miss because the Orb is its famous device, but the project name became simply World.

text: Which company led OpenAI's $40 billion funding round announced in March 2025?
explanation: SoftBank led the March 2025 $40 billion round, then the largest private tech financing, alongside Microsoft and others. Microsoft is the tempting miss because it was already the biggest backer, but this round was led by SoftBank.
